text:
emma: Heads-up: Marigold private deployment window tonight 22:00–23:30 UTC. I'll be primary deployer. Tagging @jason @priya for smoke + rollback. Plan: no DB migration, config flip, traffic shift 10%->100% over ~25m. Confirm readiness.
jason: Ack — I can smoke and monitor logs. Which endpoints + checks should I run?
emma: Smoke script: `curl -sS https://marigold.internal/health | jq .status` expect "ok". Postgres check: `psql -c 'SELECT 1'` against replica. Also check KV cache hit-rate on Dash (https://dash.company/marigold).
priya: I can run the rollout plan and preflight scripts. I'll be on-call for rollback if needed. @carlos can you stand by for any LB/network revert?
carlos: On standby. I can revert the LB rule in <5m if we need rollback. I'll join voice when we start.
emma: Deploy steps (compact):
1) push config tag `marigold-2026-03-17T22`
2) start canary @ 10% for 10m
3) run smoke.sh and health checks
4) increase to 50% for 10m
5) full cutover to 100%
Rollback quick: `deploy rollback marigold previous` then revert LB rules and config flip.
sre-bot: Reminder: maintenance window flagged in calendar. Alerts will post to #incidents if latency >200ms sustained for 5m.
jason: I'll post smoke results to this thread. Quick Q: should I warm KV before canary? I can run `warm_cache.py --keys=top1000`.
emma: :thumbsup: Yes, please warm KV and run a brief load test at 10r/s for 2m against the canary.
priya: I'll watch error budget and set temporary alert thresholds. If error rate >0.5% over 2m we rollback.
carlos: Network readiness: firewall rules updated for customer's VPC, double-checked. No further infra changes expected.
jason: Smoke run after first 10m canary:
- health: ok
- p95 latency: 120ms
- error rate: 0.08%
- DB replica lag: 0.2s
logs snippet: ```[INFO] marigold service started, health check passed```
emma: Nice. Proceeding to 50% now. ETA ~22:30 UTC.
priya: 50% stable, monitoring looks green.
emma: Cutting over to 100% now. Will ping when finished.
emma: Cutover complete. Customer reports a session resume issue — investigating. @carlos can you check LB sticky session config?
carlos: Looking now. Found missing sticky policy on one node, patching and rebalancing.
jason: Customer confirms sessions restored. All looks good on our side.
emma: Thanks team. I'll write post-deploy notes and close the window.
